# Trace fixtures

Record these fixtures with `build/threadscope`. Regenerate
from the repository root (failure/deadlock commands intentionally exit 1):

```sh
./build/threadscope run lost-update --schedule 0,1,0,1 --trace web/tests/fixtures/lost-update.json
./build/threadscope run lost-update-rmw --trace web/tests/fixtures/corrected-counter.json
./build/threadscope run mutex-deadlock --schedule 0,1 --trace web/tests/fixtures/deadlock.json
./build/threadscope run mutex-ordered --trace web/tests/fixtures/ordered-locks.json
```

Parser/navigation tests use these records. API integration tests additionally
execute the current C++ binary, so saved fixtures cannot stand in for working
backend behavior. Fixtures are never used to populate the application.

`unicode-resources.json` was generated by a temporary C++ executable linked with
`build/libthreadscope_core.a`, registering atomic resources named U+E000 and
U+10000 and encoding a zero-worker `scheduler.run()`. This reproduces the real
engine's UTF-8 name ordering, which differs from JavaScript UTF-16 comparison.
It is parser-only data for an unregistered program, never executable through
the API. Equivalent generator body:

```cpp
threadscope::AtomicInt bmp("\xee\x80\x80"), astral("\xf0\x90\x80\x80");
threadscope::Scheduler scheduler;
scheduler.track(bmp); scheduler.track(astral);
std::cout << threadscope::encode_trace({"unicode-resources/v1", 1000,
    std::chrono::milliseconds(1000), scheduler.run()});
```
